objects.text: XT1 receives the PS1 24 V DC output. AI0 records header pressure and DI a.0 reads the separate OUT1 signal.
OUT2 assumes voltage mode. Pressure scaling, OUT1 setpoints and PLC program logic remain unassigned.
XT2 exposes the normally open demand contact. The external starter, motor feeder and safety controls remain outside this drawing.
W-01 carries supply and the momentary request to DI a.1. The input requests PLC action through the program.
XT3 is the boundary for the external normally open run contact. DI a.2 reports contact state independently of the request to K1.
W-03 carries DQ a.1 and 0 V. H1 follows the PLC output command. The logic linking DI a.2 to the indication remains unassigned.
W-04 serves the external contact that closes on starter fault. DI a.3 observes the contact. Loss of the circuit is indistinguishable from an open contact.
XT5 marks the incoming L, N and PE boundary. PS1 feeds XT1. Upstream protection, conductor sizing remain unassigned.
XT6 carries PE from XT5 to the controller and starter enclosure terminal boundaries. Physical bonds, rails and conductor sizes remain unassigned.
DQ a.2 commands K2. XT7 exposes the changeover contacts. PLC alarm logic and the external annunciator supply and load remain unassigned.
W-06 serves the external contact that closes when water is available. DI a.4 is a PLC input. Sensor selection and PLC permissive logic remain unassigned.
Pressing S2 opens the DI a.5 circuit. W-07 carries the feed and return. This is a PLC operational input. Emergency-stop functions remain outside this drawing.
